reading.body:
E-Foam in Winter Garden, Florida is almost certainly not a data center, and the tag that placed it in a data center map is best treated as an error.

The evidence is the name and the setting. E-Foam reads as a foam fabrication or packaging materials business, and it sits on a light industrial street in Winter Garden where small manufacturing, fabrication, and distribution operations are the norm. A business of that kind runs ordinary office and production floor computers, an internal server closet at most. That is a different function from a building constructed to lease power, cooling, and rack space to outside tenants.

The absence of any operator record reinforces the point. No website, press mention, or business record was found describing data center, colocation, or hosting services at this address, and no power specifications are published. Florida has four facilities with published power figures totaling 9.35 MW, and this site is not among them. Among thirteen facilities mapped in the state, only a small fraction publish capacity data.

What this does not establish is what actually occupies the building. The determination rests on the name pattern and the street context, not on a confirmed business record, and the county property lookup did not return usable data. The honest reading is that this location should be removed from active tracking until independent verification shows data center operations occur there. It carries no weight in any assessment of Florida data center capacity or AI scaling.
